newsitem.title: UK: Caravaggio painting goes unsold at auction.
newsitem.headline: Caravaggio painting goes unsold at auction.

text.p: A painting attributed to Caravaggio, which was lost for 400 years, went unsold on Tuesday after failing to reach its reserve price, Phillips auctioneers said.
The oil painting of "Young Boy Peeling an Apple" was the first picture attributed to the Italian Old Master to come to auction since World War Two.
Phillips had cautiously estimated that it would fetch more than 250,000 pounds ($413,000) but other art experts had said it could sell for up to 10 million pounds.

Phillips said bidding had stopped on Tuesday at 200,000 pounds. "It is a bit disappointing," a spokeswoman told Reuters. The painting was first thought to be one of seven or more studies by pupils of Caravaggio, with the original work believed irretrievably lost.
But after examination by several leading art experts it was pronounced to be the work of the Italian master himself, painted in Rome around 1593.
The picture features a half-length figure of a boy, dressed in a cotton shirt, peeling a green fruit. It was brought to auction by a unidentified private owner.
Phillips said it was not immediately clear whether the painting would be re-submitted for auction at a later date. ($1=.6047 Pound)
